subject: GPU family selection & deal impact — proposed mapping for dedicated commit
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@valencehealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@valencehealth.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:14:00 -0500
Subject: Sizing guidance for Dedicated commit (long-context workloads)

Chloe — thanks for the sync yesterday. We’re starting to formalize the reserved-commit ask for our inference platform and need a pragmatic GPU SKU mapping that ties to our feature mix. High-level constraints:
- Production traffic: ~400 qps short interactive (<=2k tokens)
- Batch/analytics jobs: up to 30k tokens, peaks ~30 concurrent long-context inferences
- Model mix: mix of a custom 34B encoder-decoder, a few 13B generators, and embedding models for search
- Cost sensitivity: procurement wants to limit monthly committed spend and reserve burstable capacity for spikes

Can you sketch a recommended split H100/A100/L4 and the operational tradeoffs (memory headroom, batching behavior, KV cache implications)? We’ll need this to finalize the SOW.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of ML Platform, Valence Health
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@valencehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 12:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sizing guidance for Dedicated commit (long-context workloads)

Alex — quick draft below. I’ve attached a short brief and a workbook with microbenchmarks. TL;DR recommendation first, then rationale and suggested pilot steps.

TL;DR recommended mapping (initial reserved commit):
- H100 (80GB) x8 slots: primary for long-context 30k-token runs and model versions >30B that need large KV caches.
- A100 (40GB) x24 slots: baseline production for 13B–34B inference with good batching for interactive qps.
- L4 (48GB) x60 slots: embeddings, small/low-latency routing, and a burst pool for cheap rerank/fast tasks.

Why this split (brief):
- Long-context models: H100 80GB provides the simplest operational path — single-instance runs without tiling and predictable KV cache sizing. For 30k tokens and a 34B encoder-decoder, tiling is possible but complicates tail latency and cache reuse; reserving H100 avoids that complexity.
- Mid-range models: A100 (40GB) hits a sweet spot for 13B–34B if we use quantization (int8/4) and per-request batching. It offers predictable throughput per slot and lower $/token than H100 for these workloads.
- Embeddings & small models: L4 is cost-effective for high-concurrency, low-memory demands (search, rerank). Can be tiled into more instances for higher concurrency.

Operational tradeoffs and notes:
- Memory headroom: plan ~15–20% headroom on H100 for large KV caches and peak sequence lengths. A100 requires tighter headroom assumptions (10% or explicit tiling).
- Batching & latency: A100 benefits most from batching; interactive qps should be routed to A100 when latency SLO allows sub-100ms batching windows. L4 gives best P95 for tiny requests.
- Quantization: aggressive quant (int4) reduces memory but can increase hallucination risk for decoder-heavy outputs; use conservative int8 for baseline.
- Autoscaling model: Keep a small burstable pool across families; allow cross-SKU fallback (A100 -> L4 for degraded models, H100 -> A100 only for capacity constraints with model-approximation).

Next steps (recommended pilot):
1) 2-week pilot: route 25% of production to the A100 baseline and measure latency/quality.
2) Reserve H100 8-slot buffer for scheduled long-context batch jobs.
3) Enable KV prefix caching on H100 and measure cache hit curves.
4) Set up telemetry (per-token cost, P50/P95 latency, cache hit rate) and a rollback guardrail.

I’ve cc’d Dev and Karthik for capacity & price sensitivity — they can comment on commit sizing and ops playbook. I’ll follow up with a short doc we can attach to the SOW.

— Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 14:08:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Sizing guidance for Dedicated commit (long-context workloads)

Adding a few concrete operational numbers and constraints from infra side — marking up Chloe’s draft.

Assumptions (benchmarks):
- H100 80GB: ~450 tokens/s for 34B single-instance at 8 bsz; memory headroom ~20% at 30k context.
- A100 40GB: ~180 tokens/s for 34B with int8+kv-tiling at 4 bsz; better cost per token for mid workloads.
- L4 48GB: ~900 tokens/s for 13B small context workloads; optimized for concurrency and embeddings.

Commit vs burst sizing:
- For the committed reserve, price inflection is meaningful at ~12–16 reserved H100-equivalent slots or the A100-equivalent pool (committed vs burst). Given Valence’s profile, recommend committing to: H100-equivalent x8 + A100 x24 as Chloe suggested. That yields a predictable baseline and lets us offer a capped burst pool of L4s with preemptible pricing.

Tiling strategy: only use tiling for A100 when you need to run >30k contexts on constrained memory; tiling adds ~10–25ms headroom cost per tile boundary; for 30k contexts we prefer H100.

Fallback policy and quality gating:
- Route embeddings and non-quality-sensitive rerank to L4 by default.
- If A100 latency P95 > target or A100 capacity exhausted, route to L4 with a lower compute budget model and raise a ticket for remediation.

Procurement note for SOW: capture the committed baseline (H100 x8, A100 x24) and an explicit burst pool cap (L4 x60) with a monthly burst burn cap. Also include a 60-day pilot SLAs column so we can renegotiate after telemetry.

Karthik
Senior Infra Strategist, Redwood Inference

Alex — attaching the formal brief and a workbook that maps your current traffic to the proposed slots. Summary of the formal ask below and next actions to finalize SOW: 

Final recommended baseline (to include in SOW):
- Reserved: H100 (80GB) x8 slots — primary for scheduled long-context jobs and critical models >30B (KV cache friendly).
- Reserved: A100 (40GB) x24 slots — production baseline for 13B–34B models with quantization.
- Burstable pool: L4 (48GB) x60 slots — embeddings, rerank, and latency-sensitive small requests.
- Pilot & governance: 45-day telemetry window with rollback guardrails; we’ll provide a dashboard (per-token cost + P50/P95) and two quality checkpoints (after 14 days and 45 days).

Billing/ops notes:
- We’ll present two commitment bands in the SOW: (A) 12-month reserved commit with discounted unit price, (B) 3-month pilot that converts to (A) if telemetry SLOs met.
- DocuSign link to proposed SOW: https://docusign.com/Valence/commit-uid-9921

Action items:
- Valence procurement: review the attached SOW draft and confirm preferred term (3-mo pilot vs 12-mo commit).
- Alex: approve the pilot routing (25% -> A100) and confirm a list of “critical” long-context jobs to pin to H100.
- Redwood ops (Dev/Karthik): prepare slot provisioning playbook and set up cost telemetry feed.

If that all looks good I’ll push the SOW to DocuSign and schedule a kick-off.

Best — Chloe
